role.altitude: The radiologist keeps reading images, judging what history matters, conferring on diagnoses and treating complications; hunting through the record for priors, kidney function and allergies, chasing outside images by phone and burning or uploading studies by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Flagging key images for meetings while reading
role.ambitious_version: A radiologist who opens each study with priors, outside images and key history already in place.

tasks.short: Read the request, look up prior imaging, kidney function, allergies and medication, read prior reports and notes, interview the patient, phone the referring clinician when unclear, and decide what history matters to obtain patients' histories.

steps.what: Radiologist reads the request: clinical question and information from the referring clinician
Radiologist looks up prior imaging, kidney function, contrast allergy and medication in the electronic records
Radiologist reads prior reports and dictated clinical notes for relevant history
Radiologist interviews the patient before procedures
Radiologist phones the referring clinician when the history or question is unclear
Radiologist decides what in the history matters for this examination

tasks.design: A panel beside the reading worklist shows prior imaging, latest kidney function, contrast allergy and relevant medication from the record, so the radiologist does not search several screens. Prior reports and clinical notes are filtered by body region and date, but the radiologist still reads them. Reading the question, interviewing, phoning the clinician and deciding what matters stay with the radiologist. No model summarises the history.
tasks.previous_blocker: Key facts sat on different screens of the record.
tasks.still_hard: Requests with no useful clinical information.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which old finding changes the reading.
tasks.altitude: Less searching; judging the history stays.

reach.learn: Whether fewer clarifying calls are needed.

evidence.claim: Vitals, results, codes and medication can arrive by integration rather than lookup.
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of AI tools, so the panel only shows record data.

assumptions: Boundary: obtaining history; reviewing requests for nuclear medicine applicability (task 22742) and counselling patients (task 17251) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: priors in the image archive and kidney function, allergies and medication coded in the record by the lab, pharmacy and wards.
Reading the request, interviewing, phoning and deciding keep their full time.
unknowns: How well allergies are coded in the record.
research_questions: Are contrast risks missed less often?

incremental.description: Radiologist reports missing or wrong data in the panel.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much history only in free text; high: well-coded labs, allergies and priors.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Load studies with priors, review images using picture archiving systems, request outside images, check studies and recipients, and transmit images and information to other hospitals and clinicians.

steps.what: Radiologist opens the study and loads relevant priors in the picture archiving system
Radiologist reviews images and information in the picture archiving system
Radiologist requests outside images from other hospitals
Radiologist checks the study, the information to include and the recipient before sending
Radiologist transmits images and information to other hospitals or clinicians

approvals.approved_version: The study, series and accompanying information as checked by the radiologist in s4, addressed to the receiving hospital or clinician chosen there; another study or recipient needs a new check before sending.

tasks.design: Hanging protocols open each study with the relevant priors placed side by side, instead of the radiologist searching and arranging them. Outside images are requested and received through the regional image exchange network, instead of phone calls and discs. Reviewing images stays with the radiologist. After checking the study and recipient, the radiologist sends that study through the exchange network instead of exporting files or burning discs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Priors were arranged by hand and images moved on discs or by phone requests.
tasks.enabler_now: Hanging protocols and regional image exchange networks.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a subtle change between this and last year's study.

ambition.what: Compare with outside priors every time instead of only when easy to get.

tasks.altitude: Less arranging and transferring; reviewing stays.

reach.learn: Whether images arrive before the patient.

evidence.claim: Hospitals exchange images through regional networks instead of discs.
Image reading software is a certified judgement step beside a radiologist.

assumptions: Boundary: reviewing and moving images; interpreting procedures (task 17254) and checking image quality (task 22735) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s3 and s5: about 70% of partner hospitals are on the exchange network; s3 and s5 are priced at that share.
Reviewing and checking keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of partner hospitals on the network.
research_questions: Are outside priors used more often?

incremental.description: Radiologist tunes hanging protocols for new exam types.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few partners on the network; high: most partners connected and protocols tuned.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare cases and key images for multidisciplinary meetings, present them, confer with medical professionals regarding image-based diagnoses, and record the agreed conclusion.

steps.what: Radiologist prepares cases and key images for multidisciplinary meetings
Radiologist presents image-based diagnoses at the multidisciplinary meeting
Radiologist confers with medical professionals on image-based diagnoses by phone or at the workstation
Radiologist records the agreed conclusion of the meeting

tasks.design: When reading, the radiologist flags key images and adds the case to the meeting list in the picture archiving system, so preparing the meeting means opening a prepared list instead of searching each case again. Presenting and conferring stay personal. The conclusion is entered in a structured meeting form in the record, pre-filled with patient, question and imaging, instead of a free letter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cases were collected and images searched again before each meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: Meeting lists and key-image flags in the image archive.
tasks.still_hard: Cases added at the last minute.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining what an uncertain finding means for the treatment choice.

reach.learn: Whether conclusions are on record the same day.

evidence.claim: Image archives support meeting lists and key-image flags.

assumptions: Boundary: conferring on diagnoses; communicating finished results (task 17252) and writing reports (task 17242) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: key images flagged during reading under task 17254.
Presenting and conferring keep their full time.

incremental.description: Radiologist flags key images while reading.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few meetings; high: several meetings a week with many cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor the patient during and after procedures, recognize complications such as blood pressure problems, pain, oversedation or bleeding, treat them, and document them.

steps.what: Radiologist monitors the patient's vital signs and condition during and after the procedure
Radiologist recognizes complications: blood pressure problems, pain, oversedation or bleeding
Radiologist documents the complication and the treatment in the procedure record

tasks.design: Nothing changes in this task. Monitoring, recognising and treating complications stay at the bedside with the radiologist; patient monitors already alarm on set limits. s4 is part of documenting procedures, which sibling task 17248 covers; its saving is counted there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked it; this is bedside care.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a patient go pale before the monitor alarms.

evidence.claim: Patient monitors during procedures alarm on set limits for blood pressure, oxygen saturation and heart rate.

assumptions: Boundary: recognising and treating complications; documenting procedures (task 17248) is a sibling task.
s4 is the radiologist's first record of the complication and treatment and keeps its full time.
All steps keep their full time.

incremental.description: No new work; documenting complications belongs to task 17248.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
